evidence: No import-time side effects anywhere: no DB connections, file I/O, network calls, or os.environ reads at module scope in lev/*.py

lev/loop.py:11-19 computes _POSITIVE/_NEGITIVE lexicons at import time via tokenize(), but tokenize() is a pure in-memory function (regex + Counter), so import order and timing never affect the result
Import graph is strictly acyclic and shallow: cli -> {loop, router}; loop -> {engine, types}; engine -> types; __init__ -> {loop, router, types}; no conditional or lazy imports hiding cycles

No global mutable singletons; module-level state is limited to immutable-ish compiled constants (TOKEN_RE, STOPWORDS frozenset, _OVERRIDES dict, _RULES tuple) and the two frozen lexicon Counters that are never mutated after import
initialization_coupling.issues_preventing_higher_score: Import-time lexicon snapshot in loop.py couples module behavior to engine.tokenize at import; if tokenize's stemming rules ever change at runtime (they cannot today, but the pattern invites future drift), the snapshot would be stale. Also the _OVERRIDES/_RULES dicts are mutable module globals, albeit unmutated.

initialization_coupling.dimension_character: This is a small, purely computational package with essentially zero initialization surface: no environment reads, no I/O, no singleton registries, and a strict acyclic import DAG (cli -> loop -> engine -> types). The only import-time work is building two token Counters from a pure function in loop.py, which is deterministic and side-effect-free. A developer can import any module in any order without boot-order concerns.
initialization_coupling.score_rationale: Per the anchors, 90 = mostly stable with limited boot-order fragility, 100 = import any module with no worries at all. The codebase sits near the top: every module-level computation is pure and order-independent, so nothing creates real fragility. The small deduction reflects the module-level lexicon snapshot pattern (_POSITIVE/_NEGATIVE computed once at import from engine.tokenize) and the handful of mutable module-global dicts (_OVERRIDES), which are safe today but are the only seeds of the stale-snapshot class of problem this dimension guards against.

add.description: _POSITIVE/_NEGATIVE are computed once at import by calling engine.tokenize(); since tokenize is pure and the stemming rules are static, the snapshot is deterministic and safe. It is the only import-time computation in the package and would be the first place to look if tokenize ever became configurable at runtime.

All module-scope state (TOKEN_RE, STOPWORDS, _OVERRIDES, _RULES, lexicon Counters) is computed from literals via pure functions at import; there are no env reads, I/O, or network calls at module scope anywhere in the package, so imports are order-independent and test-friendly.
